strengths: Well-grounded framework with clear connection to Polya's problem-solving theory and cognitive science foundations
Dual-granularity annotation (sentence and paragraph level) reveals complementary structural insights at different reasoning scales
Comprehensive experimental design comparing diverse tasks (mathematical vs. factual reasoning) and multiple models with varying capabilities
High inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's Kappa = 0.89) demonstrating annotation quality
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (transition heatmaps and state graphs) that communicate framework utility
Interesting task-specific insights about goal-oriented mathematical reasoning vs. evidence-driven scientific reasoning
Honest acknowledgment of framework limitations including discretization, annotation bias, and fixed taxonomy constraints
weaknesses: Limited empirical scale with only 30 AIME and 50 GPQA examples—too small to support generalizable claims; lacks error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing
Annotation methodology relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini with only 10% manual verification, insufficient to validate systematic biases or ensure reproducibility across model versions

Fundamental FSM framework limitations inadequately addressed: memoryless assumption acknowledged but not explored despite potential problems for sequential reasoning; formal definition of alphabet (Σ) is non-standard and circular; transition function formalism (δ: Q × Σ → P(Q)) is defined but ignored in practice
All seven proposed applications in Discussion section (controllability, error localization, training feedback, etc.) are entirely unvalidated with zero experimental demonstration

Limited novelty: straightforward application of FSM to reasoning traces yielding primarily intuitive insights (strong models explore more, weak models finish early) with no new algorithms or control mechanisms

Methodological concerns: self-loop removal lacks justification and may lose information about reasoning redundancy; inadequate discussion of sentence vs. paragraph granularity trade-offs; highly task-specific findings with unclear generalization to other domains
Correlation vs. causation not addressed: paper shows longer FSM chains correlate with AIME accuracy but doesn't establish whether length causes performance or merely reflects model capacity
Missing ablations and comparisons: no alternative annotation schemes compared, no taxonomy ablations, no user studies validating FSM representation quality against human understanding
Lacks failure analysis: no investigation of when FSM framework breaks down or produces misleading insights for non-conforming reasoning patterns

strengths: Well-motivated FSM framework grounded in cognitive science theory (Polya) with clear formalization and mapping to LLM reasoning
Comprehensive empirical analysis across multiple models and granularities with thorough state frequency, transition probability, and FSM length metrics
Nuanced finding that reasoning optimality is task-dependent: mathematical reasoning requires longer trajectories for precision, while scientific reasoning shows saturation effects
Good reproducibility practices including detailed annotation prompts, inter-annotator agreement (0.89 Cohen's Kappa), fixed random seeds, and hyperparameter specifications
Clear presentation with well-defined six-state taxonomy and effective visualizations of state distributions and transition patterns
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope: only 80 total problems across two datasets, two task types, and three models; results may not generalize to other domains or closed-source models; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Annotation quality concerns: relies entirely on LLM auto-labeling with minimal manual verification; no analysis of annotation error patterns or their impact on conclusions; complex prompts may introduce systematic bias

Lack of practical validation: all applications in Discussion are speculative with no concrete experiments; no comparison with prior categorization work (Li et al., Bogdan et al., Lee et al.) or ablation studies showing FSM benefits

Limited theoretical depth: descriptive rather than explanatory; causality unclear between adaptive patterns and performance; memoryless FSM acknowledged but not adequately justified; discretization into 6 states loses information

Methodological limitations: self-loop removal not well justified; unclear whether six-state taxonomy is universal or inductively derived from these specific models; no analysis of how state transitions depend on reasoning history despite sequential nature

strengths: Novel FSM abstraction provides elegant bridge between interpretability and control over reasoning trajectories, addressing genuine gap in prior work

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 models, 4 benchmarks with rigorous validation: Markov assumption verified (82.1% sign agreement), annotation quality confirmed (Kappa=0.89), robustness analysis on false boundaries
Practically significant efficiency gains: 25× fewer interventions while maintaining/improving accuracy demonstrates identification of high-leverage intervention points
Thorough and honest limitations discussion including correlation-causation gap, domain specificity, cross-model generalization, and model-specific dependency
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, annotation prompts, examples of annotated CoTs provided, code availability promised
weaknesses: Fundamental correlation-causation problem remains unresolved: Transition Advantage Matrix identifies statistical associations but steering cannot compensate for model's missing domain knowledge; rescue rates vary 8.9-47.9% without clear predictive factors

State taxonomy lacks principled justification: Six states chosen post-hoc for math/science tasks with no systematic ablation on granularity; generalization to other domains speculative; Uncertainty Estimation/Backtracking distinction difficult in practice

Severe limitations on generalization: cross-model steering is 1% worse with 10× higher interventions (Table 2); distilled models show negligible gains (Table 7); domain-specific to math/science QA with binary success signals

Sentence-level granularity creates significant blind spots: 84-99.6% false boundary rates from ellipsis tokens; confidence gating mitigates but doesn't eliminate (0.1-18.9% slip-through); no principled solution offered

Q-Value iteration on noisy empirical data: requires ad-hoc reward clipping without justification; second-order analysis shows minimal benefits suggesting crude R matrix or true Markov property violation unresolved

Automated annotation bias: GPT-4o-mini used for labeling (11% disagreement rate); error propagates through pipeline; only 10% human validation; qualitative examples in Figure 3 potentially cherry-picked
Gains diminish significantly on easier tasks: +13% AIME25 vs +0.2-0.7% GSM8K; on tasks with 94%+ baseline accuracy, improvements negligible; method appears tuned to high-difficulty reasoning regimes
Missing critical comparisons: no direct comparison to Chen et al. (2025a) despite citing as motivation; no comparison to process reward models or fine-tuning baselines; unclear relative merit
